segments.title: 第88章 顏竹笙來電
segments.content:
Reignited Youth Chapter 88: A Call from Yan Zhusheng

It was the National Day holiday.

But for Lin Xiuhong and Li Guohong, there was basically no concept of a holiday in their 365-day year.

So even though it was the National Day holiday, they didn't have Li Luo come home to stay. Everything was as usual, only telling him he could come back for dinner on the evening of the 3rd, as they would have guests.

Li Luo had originally planned to go home to stay, but Ying Chanxi's computer was here now, and he needed to take advantage of the National Day holiday to write more.

So he followed his parents' arrangements.

As for Ying Chanxi, since Ying Zhicheng was still busy and wouldn't be back during the National Day holiday, it was the same for her no matter where she was.

Xu Youyu, on the other hand, had gone home after the holiday started, saying she'd come back whenever her parents started getting tired of her.

Thus, at Bihai Lanting, only Li Luo and Ying Chanxi were left.

"Li Luo, what are you doing?"

Ying Chanxi, tired from studying in her bedroom, strolled out, knocked on Li Luo's door, and pushed it open. "Watching anime again?"

"What's up?" Li Luo turned his head and asked.

"So bored."

"It's only nine in the morning, and you're already bored?"

"But we've already stayed home for three days." Ying Chanxi walked into the bedroom, plopped down on the edge of Li Luo's bed, and said while swinging her feet, "It's already the 3rd today, you're not planning to coop yourself up at home for seven days, are you?"

"That wouldn't be so bad?"

"It's a rare holiday, and you're just going to play on the computer at home every day?" Ying Chanxi gave him a light kick, annoyed. "At least go out for a walk."

"Then I'll ask Zhao Rongjun to play ball with me in the afternoon."

"Then what about me?"

"I'm discovering you're quite hard to please?" Li Luo turned his head to look at Ying Chanxi.

Even in October, Yuhang City was still very hot, without a trace of autumn.

Today, Ying Chanxi was wearing a pure white slip dress nightgown, revealing her shoulders and two fair, slender calves.

Hearing Li Luo's words, Ying Chanxi immediately pouted. "I'm asking you to take me out."

"Then you should have just said so."

"Who knew you were so dense you couldn't even figure that out."

"Alright, alright." Li Luo rolled his eyes. "But I have to go home for dinner tonight. My mom said we have guests coming over. Do you want to come with me?"

"I already made plans to have dinner with Xinyan tonight." Ying Chanxi shook her head. "Besides, your family has guests, so I won't go."

"Then I'll take you out around noon." Li Luo glanced at the time. "Come get me at eleven. We'll hang out for the afternoon, then you can go find Qiao Xinyan, and I'll go home for dinner."

"Okay," Ying Chanxi agreed happily and walked back to her own bedroom in her slippers. "I'll go read for a bit more then."

After coaxing Ying Chanxi as if she were his daughter, Li Luo once again devoted himself to the great cause of writing.

By ten in the morning, the QQ group suddenly became lively.

Because today was the 3rd, the day royalties were announced each month.

Many authors were showing off their royalty payments in the group.

In the premium author group Li Luo had just joined a few days ago, many big shots were even posting screenshots of royalties in the tens of thousands, or even hundreds of thousands.

It already broke ten thousand…

In 2014, what kind of level was a monthly income of over ten thousand?

Especially for a high school student.

Li Luo smiled, feeling quite calm inside, just a little sentimental.

When other protagonists were reborn, their first pot of gold was tens of thousands, they'd make some progress with a few hundred thousand, and a few million was just pocket change, before they went on to take down Alibaba and trample Tencent.

And here he was, happily typing away to earn a little over ten thousand yuan a month.

It could be considered hard-earned money, in a way.

But this way, he could at least lighten the family's mortgage burden a little.

Especially since this book, "I'm Really Not a Star," was doing even better than Li Luo had expected.

At over four hundred thousand words, it had an average subscription of over three thousand.

If he could steadily advance the plot and write up to a million words, and with the editor helping him get on other channels, he might be able to earn tens of thousands in royalties a month.

If he was lucky, he might even be able to pay off the mortgage ahead of schedule with just this one book.

At this thought, Li Luo slowly let out a breath.

And just then, in that premium metropolitan authors group, an author suddenly tagged him.

Li Luo clicked on it and raised his eyebrows.

That song "Annual Rings," I remember that's an original song from your book, right? @Reignited

The person who spoke was a big shot who wrote officialdom novels.

Li Luo was a little surprised, not knowing why the other person was asking this.

Reignited: I wrote it, is something the matter?

I have a friend on the female protagonist channel, and a TV series adapted from one of her books is about to air. They're selecting a theme song right now.

The production team sent over a lot of songs, and I was just casually listening along with her, but then I heard a familiar one.

I went to listen to "Annual Rings" specifically after reading it in your book. I didn't expect it to be selected as a theme song candidate.

Reignited: Huh?

You didn't know? I think it sounds great, I was even going to suggest my friend recommend it. She participated in the screenwriting this time, so she has a vote.

Reignited: It might have been recommended by my friend, I'm not too sure myself. Let me ask.

Li Luo was completely bewildered at this point.

However, he wasn't worried about plagiarism, as the song's copyright had been registered long ago.

So he just took out his phone and gave Yan Zhusheng a call, briefly explaining the situation, though he didn't mention that he was writing a novel.

Yan Zhusheng on the other end of the line was silent for a moment, then said thoughtfully, "It might be something on my mom's side. I'll ask for you."

After saying that, Yan Zhusheng hung up.

Li Luo didn't think much of it. After putting down his phone, he sent a private message to that officialdom author to get more details.

He learned that it was for a historical drama of the same name, "Immortal Fate of the Jasper Pool," adapted from a novel on the female protagonist channel.

Li Luo barely watched any TV series in his past life, so he had no impression of it.

But if "Annual Rings" had a chance to be sold, it was of course a good thing.

He just didn't know how it got selected into the production team's theme song candidate pool.

Could it be that someone on the production team was one of his readers?

As he was thinking this, there was still no news from Yan Zhusheng's end. Li Luo was no longer in the mood to continue writing, so he rarelya opened the comment section to take a look at the past month's activity.

Because he was writing a popcorn novel, Li Luo didn't have the habit of frequently checking the comment section; he didn't even look at the author's backend much.

At most, he would glance at the subscription data and the monthly royalties.

Things like reader comments, he avoided them if he could, to prevent seeing flame comments that would affect his writing mood.

But when he opened the comment section, the most conspicuous thing he saw was a thread with over a hundred replies.

Shengsheng Buxi: It's good, I prefer Mo Qinghan. Can you write more of her plotline?

When Li Luo saw the poster's nickname, he subconsciously jolted.

Then he fell into a long silence.

The phone on the desk started to vibrate.

It was a call from Yan Zhusheng.

But Li Luo was a little unsure of how to answer it.

(End of this chapter)
